name: Moonta Bay
reason: Tourism board township page names sandy coves, beaches, jetty, foreshore and Rossiters Point Lookout (Moonta/Moonta Bay/Port Hughes was SA Top Tourism Town 2021); Wikivoyage Moonta covers the same coast. A beach-and-jetty stop of half an hour or more.

name: Maitland
reason: For: tourism board page gives a historic walking trail past heritage buildings and the National Trust Museum; central town of the peninsula. Against: Wikivoyage has only a disambiguation page, no specific sight is singled out, mostly a service town.

name: Point Turton
reason: Tourism board page: 1876 jetty (still used by fishers), white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, boating and diving; a second-tier seaside stop. Beach and jetty are one place (Point Turton Beach is a duplicate).

name: Corny Point
reason: Tourism board page names surf breaks (Rock Pool, Salmon Hole, Daly Head, Berry Bay), three swimming beaches and the Corny Point to Berry Bay coastal drive; visitors beaches stop. Lighthouse is a separate candidate.

name: Black Point
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage (own section with Pine Point, "one of the most gorgeous stretches of coastline") and the tourism board page (safe white-sand beach with no rips, crabbing, swimming).

name: Stenhouse Bay Lookout Walk
reason: parks.sa.gov.au lists it as an easy 1 hour, 2 km cliff-top loop with views over Investigator Strait "among the best in the park"; a distinct walk from the jetty car park.

name: Thomson-Pfitzner Plaster Trail
reason: Agency-listed 3 hour, 7.6 km hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay with interpretive signs; Wikivoyage lists it too (though calls it the least interesting trail). Objection: overlaps the Inneston ruins, a plain track.

name: Gym Beach Hike
reason: Agency-listed 4 hour, 9.8 km hike through dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach; Wikivoyage calls it the longest trail in the park.

name: Investigator Strait Shipwreck Trail
reason: Heritage trail named by the SA government, southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au (interpretive signs around the southern coast from Edithburgh to Innes, including the Ethel wreck). Objection: mainly a dive trail, spread over many sites.

name: Dolphin Beach
reason: Named as a beach to visit in Innes National Park by the Tourism Australia G'day Parks guide (and photographed by southaustralia.com); sits on the Royston Head road. Objection: parks.sa.gov.au gives it only a passing mention, so a single guide source.

name: Moonta Rainbow and Flower Murals
reason: Rule 3: one mural on a cafe wall and a painted footpath on Ellen Street (yorkepeninsula.com.au listing); the visit is minutes. The broader Moonta Art Trail is the thing a guide names, not this single artwork.

name: Wallaroo Mines
reason: Rule 1/3: searched yorkepeninsula.com.au, Wikivoyage Kadina/Wallaroo and council heritage pages; no visitor source names Wallaroo Mines as a stop, only as sites (ruins, cemetery) on the Kadina Heritage Trail and Copper Rail Trail. Moonta Mines is the real mining stop.

name: Hillside Mine
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source after searching tourism board, Wikivoyage and parks pages; a former mine site with no visitor offering.

name: Map the Miner
reason: Outside the region: belongs to the region covering Kapunda (about -34.35, 138.91); no counted source found either.

name: Port Broughton Heritage Centre and Museum
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Port Broughton, $7 entry; yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Broughton page); a permanent venue, small hours do not make it an event. Objection: open only Tue and Thu 1-3 pm.

name: Bublacowie Military Museum
reason: Two sources: visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (extensive WWI/WWII/Vietnam collection, memorial gardens, tours) and History SA; guided visits last an hour or two. Objection: private museum, open Sun to Tue or by appointment.

name: Port Victoria Maritime Museum
reason: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Victoria page and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the windjammer grain-race story). Objection: open weekends 2-4 pm only.

name: Bird Islands Conservation Park
reason: Rule 2: offshore islands and a mangrove mainland section; the regional tourism page only restates its size and location, with no visit, walk or facility named. Searched Wikivoyage, parks.sa.gov.au and visityorkepeninsula.com.au.

name: Bute Fauna Park
reason: For: southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au list it; free, volunteer-run, emus, kangaroos, peacocks and picnic shelters, a break on the journey. Against: one source type, small enclosure park, a visit of under half an hour for most.

name: Point Turton Beach
reason: Duplicate of Point Turton (the township page covers the jetty and beach as one place).

name: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Minlaton and the yorkepeninsula.com.au Minlaton page (the only genuine Red Devil monoplane, first airmail over the sea, free display on the edge of town).

name: Corny Point Lighthouse
reason: Listed as an attraction by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com; an 1882 lighthouse reserve reached by Lighthouse Road with a picnic area and coast to linger on; Wikivoyage names it too. Free, self-guided.

name: Chinamans Hat Island
reason: Rule 2: offshore rock island with no public landing; not named by Wikivoyage, parks.sa.gov.au or the tourism board.

name: Ardrossan Heritage Museum
reason: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (in the old Smith stump-jump plough factory, shipwreck Zanoni display, open seven days 10-4).

name: Stansbury Museum
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Stansbury See; visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page): 1878 schoolroom with farm and industry displays. Objection: volunteer-run, open Wed and Sun afternoons.

name: Edithburgh Museum
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Edithburgh See (adults $3) and the visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (salt industry, shipwrecks, produce-store building). Objection: weekend afternoons only.

name: Edithburgh Jetty
reason: Wikivoyage lists it as its own destination (dive site), and the tourism board says it is renowned for diving and snorkelling with seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons; a jetty walk and shore dive a visitor goes for.

name: Troubridge Hill Lighthouse
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage only mentions it in passing as a working light; parks.sa.gov.au, tourism board give no visit. A working lighthouse not open to visitors (the visitable Troubridge Island is separate).

name: Wool Bay Jetty and Lime Kilns
reason: Tourism board page names the uniquely designed lime kilns on the cliff top and the old port jetty, with a lookout; a free heritage stop on the coast road. Objection: a short stop, one source.

name: Coobowie Aquatic Reserve
reason: Rule 1/2: marine reserve with no visitor facility or walk named by the tourism board, Wikivoyage or parks pages.

name: Yorketown Pink Lakes
reason: Tourism board and southaustralia.com name the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail (self-drive routes, boardwalk at Par Lake, Pink Lake viewing platform, 15 to 90 min). Objection: lake colour varies by season, and it could duplicate a Salt Lake Trail candidate.

name: Wattle Point Wind Farm
reason: Rule 1/2: operating wind farm, no visitor facility named by any tourism source (Wikivoyage mentions it only as a beach walk landmark).

name: Leven Beach Conservation Park
reason: Rule 2: the regional tourism page only gives size, vegetation and location (no walk, lookout or facility named), parks.sa.gov.au does not list it and Wikivoyage names it only in a list.

reason: Rule 1: searched the tourism board, visityorkepeninsula.com.au beaches page and Wikivoyage; no visitor source names it.

name: Tiddy Widdy Beach
reason: For: tourism board page names the CH Smith Trail (3 km clifftop walk to Ardrossan) and crabbing/beach. Against: a small holiday settlement, the page lists no attraction, only one source, and the trail is a separate walk.

name: Cape Elizabeth
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source names the cape or a thing to do there (searched the tourism board townships and beaches pages).
